newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia bonds pare fall on inflation view.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia bonds pare fall on inflation view.

text.p: *Australian bonds reined back the earlier price falls in response to the the Reserve Bank's positive inflation outlook.
*However, the RBA Bulletin also said current monetary policy was appropriate and it remains wary on wages outcomes.
The RBA also said that current monetary policy settings were broadly appropriate and went to great lengths to emphasise its concerns over future wage claims.
However, the impact on the market from these remarks was slightly watered down following similar comments by RBA governor Ian Macfarlane last week.

"All the RBA has done is expand on what Macfarlane was saying last week. Obviously they are still happy with the inflation outlook, but there is an awful lot about wages," said Stephen Roberts, chief economist at UBS Australia.

The RBA said wage costs needed to be contained for economic recovery to be sustained, and while results over 1996 have been satisfactory, outcomes from enterprise bargaining in the private sector seem to be higher than aggregate inflation.

"A rise in other types of wages, which pushed them near to the increases achieved in enterprise agreements, would lead to an aggregate wage outcome which was inconsistent with the inflation objective, and so have implications for future monetary policy," it added.
It also said that the trade unions "living wage" claim could adversely affect employment.
UBS's Roberts said there was certainly nothing in the report to suggest that the bank had an easing bias.
"The way I read it is that monetary policy is on hold for a long time, but with a sort of tightening bias when you look further out," he added.

Such a bias is already being priced in the bill futures structure with the December 1997 bill futures already nearly pricing in a 50 basis-point tightening in current official 6.0 percent official interest rates by maturity.

The local market's recovery saw spreads to the dollar bloc show a modest outperformance, although domestic turnover was relatively light after Monday's U.S. holiday. Canadian bonds were flat on Monday ahead of the Canadian federal budget later today, while New Zealand debt continued to underperform.
